observation.visible_scene: A coastal beach at a low sun (dusk or dawn). The sun sits near the horizon in the center-left, partly veiled by overcast clouds. On the right a dark cliff rises, topped by a light-colored house. The sea fills the middle ground with a vertical, shimmering column of sun-reflection running down to the foreground. The lower edge shows a dark pebble/sand beach. The framing of the horizon, cliff, house and sun stays fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: The camera is effectively static: the cliff, house, sun and horizon hold the same positions throughout, so apparent motion is scene motion, not camera motion.
A small wave rolls shoreward: a faint crest line first becomes visible in the lower-left/center water around the middle frames and translates diagonally toward the beach in later frames.

That wave crest steepens and breaks into a line of white foam along the water's edge in the lower-left/center (most evident in the last third of the clip), i.e. the breaking is a deformation of the same advancing wave, not a separate object.

The sun's reflection column persists continuously, its bright patch and vertical streak shimmering and wobbling slightly as the surface ripples, but it does not move horizontally as an independent object.
A thin residual foam line remains at the right side of the beach throughout, distinct from the new breaking wave on the left.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the breaking wave fully washes up the beach and then recedes after the last frame.
Whether the sun is rising or setting (position barely changes within this short excerpt).
Any earlier wave cycle before the first frame and the overall tide state.
uncertain_details: Any drift of the cloud layer is too subtle to confirm against the static horizon.
Exact frame at which the incoming wave first forms its crest is gradual and not sharply defined.
The shimmering reflection cannot be separated into discrete moving glints; it reads as one continuous column modulated by ripples.
